D.t: Angie Nixon trails by 4.6 and wins 20% of simulations. Closing it takes about 206,749 voters switching sides, or 413,499 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +11.8 and D +2.6. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +5.6. Your best recent poll is St. Pete Polls at R +1.7; your worst is YouGov for N+ Univision at R +10.1. 23 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Broward, a projected net 211,750 votes; Orange, a projected net 117,176 votes; Palm Beach, a projected net 68,041 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Miami-Dade, D +3.0, 9.2% of the vote; Palm Beach, D +11.0, 6.9% of the vote; Hillsborough, D +5.2, 6.3% of the vote; Pinellas, D +3.8, 5.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Angie Nixon runs furthest behind in Sumter, Collier, Marion. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 79% of voters, 50 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.96 points; White voters, 69% of voters, 39 to 59, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.46 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 67% of voters, 47 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.35 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Angie Nixon: Immigration voters 18 to 79, Midsize counties 38 to 59, White voters 39 to 59. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$265K cash against $8.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Registered Democrats cast 38% of the 4,717,903 ballots in Florida so far, against 41% for the other party. That is 7.3 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 2.1 points away from Angie Nixon. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Activity: 5 campaign stops by the candidate or surrogates in 30 days.

R.t: Ashley Moody leads by 4.6 in the forecast and wins 80% of simulations. The cushion is about 413,499 votes; a one point swing is about 44,654 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +2.6 and R +11.8. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +5.6. Your best recent poll is YouGov for N+ Univision at R +10.1; your worst is St. Pete Polls at R +1.7. 23 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Lee, a projected net 73,132 votes; Collier, a projected net 53,641 votes; Marion, a projected net 47,228 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Miami-Dade, D +3.0, 9.2% of the vote; Palm Beach, D +11.0, 6.9% of the vote; Hillsborough, D +5.2, 6.3% of the vote; Pinellas, D +3.8, 5.1% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Ashley Moody runs furthest behind in Miami-Dade, Broward, Duval. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 79% of voters, 47 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.96 points; White voters, 69% of voters, 59 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.46 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 67% of voters, 51 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.35 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Ashley Moody: Black voters 19 to 78, Independents 26 to 69, Moderates 33 to 64. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$8.5M cash against $265K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
